title: Cognition Sales Play: Devin, the autonomous AI software engineer
positioning: Devin is not another coding assistant. It is an autonomous AI software engineer that plans, executes, tests, and ships production-ready work, turning engineering backlogs, migrations, security remediation, and on-call into measurable output instead of capacity constraints.
oneliner: Assistants make developers faster. Devin makes the engineering organization larger, without the headcount.
closing: This play positions Cognition as the company that turns AI from a coding productivity tool into actual engineering capacity. Use the proof points aggressively and always bring the conversation back to measurable throughput and risk reduction.

primary: Mid-to-large engineering organizations (100 to 5,000+ engineers) with significant technical debt, migration backlogs, or security vulnerability queues
Companies already investing heavily in AI coding tools (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) but still bottlenecked on execution capacity
Security and platform teams drowning in scanner findings that never get fixed
Organizations running frequent on-call rotations or high-incident environments
secondary: High-growth startups scaling engineering faster than they can hire
Enterprises undergoing major platform modernization (monolith to services, database migrations, framework upgrades)
icp.energy: Every target account fits the primary profile: large engineering estates, active ERP and integration programs, cost programs with workforce reductions, and OT-adjacent security exposure. Add the energy buying centers from the Pain by altitude chapter: CIO, Chief Technology and Engineering Officer, Digital presidents at the oilfield services companies, and program sponsors for ERP and integration work.

diff.text: Copilot is an excellent pair programmer that lives in the IDE. Devin is an autonomous teammate that lives in the backlog. Copilot amplifies individual developers; Devin multiplies team throughput on well-scoped work. Most sophisticated teams run both: Copilot for daily flow and Devin for delegated execution.

diff.vs: Anthropic OSS Scanner and Claude Security
diff.text: The OSS Scanner is strong at discovery on public open-source projects. Devin owns the private-codebase loop: discover, validate exploitability in a sandbox, write the patch, open the PR. They are complementary, not competitive.

discovery.q: Where is engineering capacity currently the biggest constraint: feature velocity, tech debt, security remediation, or migrations?
How large is your current vulnerability backlog, and what percentage of high and critical findings actually get fixed in a reasonable window?
What major migrations or platform modernizations are planned or already underway?
How much senior engineer time is spent on on-call investigation versus product work?
Which AI coding tools are already in use, and what work still requires full human ownership of the loop?
If you could 5-10x the throughput on a specific class of work (security fixes, migrations, debt cleanup), what would that unlock for the business?

pitch.say: Most teams have already adopted AI coding assistants. The next question is: what work can you actually delegate instead of just accelerate?
pitch.energy: Add the altitude: for an executive, tie delegation to the savings or integration commitment.

pitch.say: Frame the capacity, security, migration, and on-call pains using their language.
pitch.energy: Use the account's pain chain and its implication sequence from Scoping.

pitch.say: Position Devin as the autonomous engineer. Contrast assistant versus teammate. Highlight Security Swarm and Oncall as high-ROI entry points.
pitch.energy: Mention Windows machines and Teams for Microsoft-heavy estates.

pitch.say: Walk one or two relevant case studies with hard numbers. Emphasize: review the PR, don't own the process.
pitch.energy: Nubank for migrations, AngelList for on-call and data platforms.

pitch.say: Explicitly address Copilot and Anthropic offerings. Position as complementary where true.
pitch.energy: Most energy majors have a Microsoft agreement; position alongside Copilot, not against it.

pitch.say: The teams getting the most leverage treat Devin like a new class of engineering capacity, not another tool. Let's identify one high-value workflow and run a focused pilot.
pitch.energy: Following McMahon, propose scoping first: quantify the workflow, then a go/no-go with the economic buyer before the POV.

objections.o: We already have Copilot, Cursor or Claude Code
objections.r: Great. Those make individual developers faster. Devin makes the team faster by owning end-to-end work. Most of our best customers run both.

objections.o: AI-generated code still needs heavy review
objections.r: Correct. Devin is designed for human review of finished PRs, not unsupervised production pushes. The value is collapsing the time from ticket to reviewable PR.
Most scanners create findings. Security Swarm creates validated, exploit-confirmed findings plus the remediation PR. That's the missing half of the loop.

objections.o: Too expensive, or usage will explode
objections.r: We now have efficiency-based controls that raise limits for high-output users and surface low-efficiency usage. Customers actively manage ROI, not just spend.

objections.o: Our codebase is too complex or proprietary
objections.r: Devin is used on multi-million-line monoliths and highly regulated environments. The parallel agent architecture (Agentic MapReduce) was built exactly for this.

options: Security vulnerability backlog clearance (highest emotional and measurable ROI)
A concrete migration or large-scale refactor
metrics: Reduction in open high and critical vulnerabilities
pilot.energy: Run it as McMahon's proof of value: the 30-45 days sit inside the Proof of value phase of the mutual action plan, and the success metrics come straight from the cost justification.

Run a paid pilot with clear success criteria
Executive briefing for the CTO or VP Engineering on capacity multiplication strategy
